output.hypothesis: The current list_notes implementation fetches all notes and filters them in Python, causing O(N) I/O and CPU usage. By moving filtering to SQL using LIKE for text search and IN for tags, we reduce data transfer and Python-side processing. This aligns with the profile showing high time in list_notes and _make_note due to processing all rows.
risks: SQL injection if search_text contains special characters, but parameterized queries prevent this.
LIKE with wildcards may be slower than full-text search for very large datasets, but for typical note counts, it's efficient.
The IN clause with many tags might hit SQL limits, but tag counts are typically small.
